title: Tanks, aircraft and museums.
text: Personal website · Jorge Puente García Tanks, aircraft and museums. I like tanks and combat aircraft. I have visited few museums, but I follow their collections and enjoy discovering vehicles in films and video games. In War Thunder, I take a collecting approach: I am drawn to the detail with which it represents and explains tanks and aircraft. title: About me
text: About me Hi, I am Jorge Puente García I have a degree in Computer Engineering from the University of Oviedo and am currently studying for a master’s degree in Web Engineering. I work as a software developer at TWave, focusing on backend development, web interfaces and industrial communications. Outside work, I am interested in tanks, aircraft and how they appear in films and video games. title: Vehicles and museums
text: Vehicles and museums I have selected four vehicles I enjoy studying: two tanks, an anti-aircraft vehicle and a fighter. Enlarge the photographs and expand each card to learn why they interest me. T-90M Main battle tank Why it interests me With the T-90M, I enjoy looking at how protection, mobility and armament are combined. Comparing it with other tanks helps me understand its development. Photo credit and licence Strela-10 Air defence Why it interests me The Strela-10 interests me because it puts air defence on tracks. I find its ability to move alongside other vehicles interesting. Photo credit and licence Su-57 Military aviation Why it interests me The Su-57's silhouette catches my attention. I enjoy comparing the design decisions behind a fighter with those behind a ground vehicle. Photo credit and licence T-72 The Tank Museum Why it interests me Seeing this T-72 on display helps me picture its actual size. I like how the museum goes beyond specifications to explain its history. Photo credit and licence Museums I follow I follow these museums because they present vehicles in context, beyond their specifications. title: Help and site map
text: Help and site map Site map Home About me Vehicles and museums Video and podcast Films and TV series Video games Search How to use this website Press Tab to move to the next link or control, and Shift + Tab to go back. Activate them with Enter; buttons also support Space. The first link lets you skip to the main content. In carousels, use the buttons, swipe, or press the left and right arrow keys when the carousel is focused. They do not advance automatically. In enlarged photographs, use Close image or Escape to return. The menu indicates your current section. You can switch between Spanish and English in the header. Something not working? If audio or video does not play, use its download link. If a link is broken or you need content in another format, email uo294228@uniovi.es with the page address and a description of the problem. Adjust reading to your preferences Press the floating Accessibility button in the bottom corner of any page. A panel opens with text up to 200%, the OpenDyslexic font for dyslexia, spacing, simple headings, highlighted links and reduced motion. Try the settings and choose what feels comfortable. OpenDyslexic is optional and applies across the website; it takes priority over the simple heading font. Close settings or Escape closes the panel and returns focus to the button. Reset settings restores the original design and removes saved preferences. Settings are optional, saved locally and shared across pages and both languages in this browser. They are not sent to any service. If storage is blocked, they work for the current page visit. Without JavaScript, you can still navigate and use browser zoom and accessibility features.
